products.name: ROVER IDPA Belt
products.summary: A 1.5-inch articulated competition gun belt for IDPA shooters, built around the 2026 IDPA rulebook.
products.description: The R.O.V.E.R. IDPA Belt is a 1.5-inch articulated competition gun belt built for IDPA shooters and configured to conform to the rules in the 2026 IDPA rulebook. It's designed to be manufactured on a consumer FDM printer and assembled with inexpensive off-the-shelf hardware, so it can be built entirely at home or ordered finished. Instead of a traditional fiber or nylon belt, **hinged links** conform around your waist while still giving your holster, magazine pouches, and other accessories a rigid platform. The links are made from a high-strength polymer blend selected for rigidity, durability, and resistance to temperature, humidity, and impact, and they are joined with M2 × 35 mm spring pins. A **ratcheting closure** lets you dial in belt tension quickly and release it just as easily, and because links can be added, removed, or individually replaced, the belt is simple to size, maintain, and repair. No traditional inner/outer belt system required. Under the 2026 IDPA rulebook, belts may not exceed **1.75 inches (44.45 mm)** in width or **5/16 inch (7.94 mm)** in thickness, and this design fits comfortably within both limits. None of this is theoretical. Klock Holding Co.'s own belt has been through roughly 30 IDPA matches without a broken or cracked link, walking pin, or measurable hinge wear, and R.O.V.E.R. belts are in use by competitors with different waist sizes, body types, and equipment configurations. Each belt can be made in a variety of colors and textures, with multiple link sizes and a 0.75 link to dial in the fit for your hips. Nothing beyond the ratchet kit is proprietary: the links print at home, and every other part is bought off the shelf.

makerBlocks.label: Assembly
steps: Orient each link with the reduced pin bore facing downward.
Assemble the links and insert an M2 × 35 mm spring pin from the top.
Drive the pin until it sits flush with the top surface.
With a 1/16 in punch, lightly seat the pin until it bottoms against the reduced bore.
Repeat until the belt reaches the length you need.
makerBlocks.note: Each hinge has one reduced-diameter pin bore that works as both the installation stop and the access point for pin removal. To remove a pin, insert the punch into that bore from the bottom of the link and drive the pin upward. The opening can be tight at first — that's intentional, so the pin stays retained.

makerBlocks.label: Compatibility
notes: These links are **not** compatible with DAA Lynx components. Both systems use articulated links, but the pin diameter, hinge spacing, and overall geometry are different enough that parts from the two can't be mixed.
The belt is built around Tek-Lok connectors and pairs with the ROVER mounting plates and accessories.

makerBlocks.label: Care and maintenance
notes: A little lubricant worked between the rotating joints noticeably improves articulation and makes the belt easier to put on, take off, and adjust while wearing. Use something compatible with your filament.
Replace a single link instead of the whole belt when something wears out. Pins push out with the same punch used to install them.
Keep a few spare spring pins on hand. They cost almost nothing and a belt can be back in service in minutes.

products.name: ROVER USPSA Belt
products.summary: A 1.5-inch articulated competition gun belt for USPSA, with thicker links and more mounting options than the IDPA version.
products.description: The ROVER USPSA Belt is a 1.5-inch articulated competition gun belt designed and optimized for USPSA. It's designed to be manufactured on a consumer FDM printer and assembled with inexpensive off-the-shelf hardware, so it can be built entirely at home or ordered finished. Instead of a traditional fiber or nylon belt, **hinged links** conform around your waist while providing a rigid platform for your holster, magazine pouches, and other accessories. The links are made from a high-strength polymer blend selected for rigidity, durability, and resistance to temperature, humidity, and impact. A **ratcheting closure** lets you quickly dial in belt tension and release it just as easily, and links can be added, removed, or individually replaced, making the belt simple to size, maintain, and repair. The articulated design provides a secure setup that mates to your existing inner velcro belt. The USPSA version has many more link options than the IDPA version, including direct-through, mount-to, and in-between sized links, so attachments can mount to and through the belt. The links are also **30% thicker**, providing a very rigid, stable, and strong platform for your gear, and the belt rolls up. None of this is theoretical. R.O.V.E.R. USPSA belts are in use by active competitors with different waist sizes, body types, and equipment configurations, and each belt can be made in a variety of colors and textures with multiple link sizes available to dial in the fit for your hips. Nothing beyond the ratchet kit is proprietary: the links print at home, and every other part is bought off the shelf.

products.name: ASTRO Magazine Pouch
products.summary: A modular magnetic magazine pouch you can print in matching or contrasting colors.
products.description: ASTRO is a modular magnetic magazine pouch: every part prints on its own, so you can build it in matching or contrasting colors and swap a single part instead of rebuilding the whole pouch. It holds the magazine with a magnet rather than a mechanical latch, so the draw is fast and there's nothing to defeat on the way out. It mounts with **Tek-Lok Mini** compatible attachments or the **KlockLok** connector, and it uses common M4 and M2 hardware and the same 25–26 mm countersunk neodymium cup magnets used in the other magnetic pouches. Because the body, backplate, and sides are separate pieces, the pouch is easy to repair and easy to adapt: right now it's set up for **Glock magazines**, and more bodies are coming.

products.name: GROMIT Magnet Attachment
products.summary: A compact, magnet-retained magazine holder for make-ready and other competition-use positions.
products.description: The GROMIT Magnetic Mag Holder is an administrative, magnet-retained holder for a make-ready magazine or another non-retention-critical competition position. It combines a rigid PETG inner body with a TPU outer shell: the PETG core supports the magnet, carries the structural loads, and provides the mounting interface, while the TPU shell protects the magnet assembly, improves durability, and absorbs minor impacts. It uses inexpensive off-the-shelf hardware and attaches to a Mini 2-Hole Tek-Lok compatible mount with M4 socket-head cap screws and hex nuts, so it fits a wide range of competition belt attachment systems. Use one 32 mm countersunk neodymium cup magnet for most steel-bodied magazines, or two magnets for Glock polymer-bodied magazines where less steel is exposed. It's intended for competition and administrative handling—not duty, field, or concealed-carry retention.

steps: Print the inner body in PETG.
Print the outer shell in TPU.
Install the magnet(s) into the PETG body.
Press the M4 hex nuts into the printed hex pockets.
Secure the assembly using M4 socket head cap screws.

makerBlocks.note: The printed hex pockets are designed as a light press fit — gently tap the nuts into place before installing the screws if needed. Fastener length isn't critical: any M4 screw between approximately 6 mm and 10 mm that provides adequate thread engagement without bottoming out should function correctly.

makerBlocks.label: Magnet configuration
makerBlocks.note: A single magnet provides adequate retention for most steel-bodied magazines. Glock magazines benefit from a second magnet because the polymer body reduces the amount of exposed steel available for magnetic attraction, which lowers holding force.

makerBlocks.label: Compatibility and testing
notes: **Tested:** factory Glock pistol magazines in every currently produced caliber, including 9×19, .40 S&W, .357 SIG, .45 GAP, 10 mm Auto, and .45 ACP.

**Tested:** fully loaded Glock 9 mm magazines with +5 aluminum extensions from Henning Group and Taran Tactical Innovations (TTI), securely retained in the two-magnet configuration during normal movement and range use.
**Tested:** both competition orientations, with cartridges facing toward the body (“bullets in”) and away from it (“bullets out”). Both configurations function without modification.
**Verified:** Mini 2-Hole Tek-Lok compatible mounting pattern.
Retention recommendations are based on practical range testing rather than instrumented pull-force measurements.

makerBlocks.label: Future development
notes: Future revisions might add more mounting patterns, support for other magnet sizes, and variants for more magazine families. I'll test non-Glock magazines as those platforms come available.
